hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? ever messed up so badly you didn’t think you could go back?
options: most of us have. hold onto that feeling. this story was told for it.
then keep them in mind while you hear this one.
good. just listen. you might need this one later, or someone you love might.

steps.line: Jesus told a story. A young man said to his father, “Give me my share of what’s coming to me.”

steps.q: Back then, you got your share when your father died. So asking for it now was a bit like saying…
o: “I’m ready to grow up.”
“I wish you were gone.”
“Help me start a business.”
steps.why: That’s how many readers hear it: a deep insult. Now watch what the father does.

steps.line: So the father divided what he had.
Not many days later, the younger son packed everything and left for a far country.
There he wasted it all on wild living.
Then a severe famine came over that country, and he began to be in need.
He took a job feeding pigs. He longed to eat what the pigs ate, and no one gave him anything.

steps.q: Jesus’s listeners would have winced at the pigs. Why?
o: Pigs were sacred animals
Under Jewish law, pigs were unclean
Only slaves worked with animals
steps.why: Jesus was speaking to Jewish listeners. Feeding pigs for a foreigner was about as low as a Jewish son could fall.

steps.q: You’re starving in a far country, feeding pigs. Luke says one thought tipped him toward home. Which?
o: How kind his father always was
That his brother might take him back
That his father’s hired hands eat well
steps.why: Luke 15:17: “My father’s hired servants have bread to spare, and I’m dying of hunger.” His reason was his stomach, not his heart, and the father welcomes him anyway.

steps.line: He set off for home, practicing his speech: “Father, I have sinned. Make me one of your hired servants.”

steps.q: Why does he plan to ask to be a servant, not a son?
o: He felt he’d lost the right to be a son
His father had said he’d disown him
His brother had taken his place
steps.why: Luke 15:19: “I am no longer worthy to be called your son.” Some scholars add he hoped to earn back what he’d lost as a hired man. Hold onto that.

steps.line: But while he was still far off, his father saw him.

steps.q: His father sees him on the road. What does he do?
o: Waits at the door, arms crossed
Sends a servant to ask why he’s back
Runs to him
steps.why: He runs. In that culture a grown man running in public was undignified. He didn’t care.

steps.line: He was moved with compassion. He ran, threw his arms around him, and kissed him.
The son began his speech. The father didn’t let him finish.

steps.q: The father cuts him off. Which line of his practiced speech never gets said?
o: “Father, I have sinned.”
“I’m not worthy to be your son.”
“Make me one of your hired servants.”
steps.why: Luke 15:21, in most translations: he gets through “not worthy” but never reaches the servant part. The father answers with orders for a robe, a ring and sandals.

steps.label: Luke 15:22-24
steps.line: “Bring out the best robe. Put a ring on his hand. Let’s celebrate. He was lost, and is found.”

steps.q: Each gift said something. Match them.
pairs: honor: the finest in the house
steps.why: A servant would get none of these. Each gift undoes the speech he practiced, before he could finish it.

say: here’s the part i love. the son had a whole speech ready. his father never heard the end of it.
christians read the father as a picture of God. not waiting at the door with a lecture. running down the road.

steps.q: Luke says Jesus told this story to people complaining that he welcomed sinners. Who was it really for?
o: The sinners, so they’d behave
The complainers, who weren’t glad
His friends, as a warning about money
steps.why: Luke 15 opens with religious leaders grumbling about the company Jesus kept. The story keeps going for them: the older brother, who won’t come to the party.

today.say: is there someone you’ve drifted from? today, send one short, kind message. no speech needed.
options: that’s the whole thing. one step down the road.
Someone came to mind, not today
that counts too. keep them in mind. the door stays open.
